claims.text: GDACS's event report for Tropical Cyclone Simon (event id 1001335, episode 32) rates the event an Overall Orange alert, running 07 Oct 2026 15:00 UTC to 15 Oct 2026 09:00 UTC, with maximum sustained winds of 250 km/h (Category 4) per NOAA model data, a medium humanitarian impact and medium vulnerability for Mexico, and a maximum forecast storm surge of 0.5 m.

NOAA's National Hurricane Center Public Advisory 32 for Tropical Storm Simon, issued 200 AM MST (0900 UTC) on 15 October 2026, reports maximum sustained winds of 60 mph (95 km/h), minimum central pressure of 996 mb, a nearly stationary position near 19.2N 108.5W (about 270 miles SSE of Cabo San Lucas), no coastal watches or warnings in effect, and rainfall totals of 1-2 inches (isolated 3 inches) forecast for Baja California Sur through early Saturday.

NOAA's National Hurricane Center Advisory 56 for Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel, issued 8:00 PM PDT (0300 UTC) on 10-11 October 2026, reports maximum sustained winds of 60 mph (95 km/h), a minimum central pressure of about 987 mb, a position near 30.0N 116.5W (about 40 miles west of Punta Baja, Mexico, and 190 miles south of San Diego) moving north-northeast at about 36 mph, with tropical-storm-force winds extending up to 140 miles from the center.

NOAA's National Hurricane Center's final public advisory (No. 38) for Simon, issued 2:00 PM MST on 16 October 2026, reports Simon has dissipated into a remnant low near 21.5N 110.3W (about 100 miles south-southwest of Cabo San Lucas), with maximum sustained winds weakened to about 35 mph and minimum central pressure near 1006 mb, moving northwest at about 13 mph; no coastal watches or warnings are in effect, though swells could produce life-threatening surf and rip currents along parts of western Mexico and Baja California Sur.

description: Hurricane Simon and Tropical Storm Rachel struck Mexico's Pacific coast and Baja California between 7 and 16 October 2026, prompting a GDACS Overall Orange alert for Simon and a multi-state emergency response. GDACS and NOAA recorded Simon peaking at Category 4 strength with sustained winds of 250 km/h before weakening; Rachel moved inland over northern Baja California as a post-tropical system on 10-11 October before dissipating over the southwestern United States. NOAA's National Hurricane Center declared Simon dissipated into a remnant low on 16 October, with no coastal watches or warnings in effect, though swells continued to pose a surf and rip-current hazard along western Mexico's coast. No authoritative casualty or displacement figure has been published by GDACS or NOAA for either system.

impact.summary: GDACS's event report for Hurricane Simon rated it an Overall Orange alert with medium humanitarian impact at its Category 4 peak (250 km/h sustained winds). NOAA's National Hurricane Center's final advisory (No. 38, 2:00 PM MST, 16 October) declared Simon dissipated into a remnant low near Cabo San Lucas with winds down to about 35 mph and no coastal watches or warnings in effect, though dangerous swells persisted along western Mexico's coast. Post-tropical cyclone Rachel had already dissipated over the southwestern United States after moving inland over northern Baja California on 10-11 October. Neither GDACS nor NOAA has published a confirmed death toll or displacement figure for either system.

location.region: Pacific coast states (Guerrero, Jalisco, Colima, Michoacan, Nayarit) and Baja California/Baja California Sur

event.scale: Simon peaked Category 4 (250 km/h), dissipated 16 Oct; Rachel dissipated as post-tropical system

name: Hurricane Simon and Tropical Storm Rachel, Mexico

updates.text: NOAA's National Hurricane Center declared Simon dissipated into a remnant low in its final advisory (No. 38, 2:00 PM MST, 16 October), with winds down to about 35 mph near Cabo San Lucas and no coastal watches or warnings in effect; Rachel had already dissipated as a post-tropical system on 10-11 October. Both systems are now resolved with no confirmed casualty or displacement figures published.
